headline: World Life Expectancy Rebounds to Nearly Pre-Pandemic Heights
meta_description: Global life expectancy has bounced back to 73.3 years in 2023, nearly matching 2019 levels. But healthy life expectancy still lags behind.
summary_short: Global life expectancy has nearly recovered to pre-pandemic levels at 73.3 years in 2023, though the challenge remains ensuring those years are lived in good health.
body:
The world has made a significant stride in bouncing back from pandemic setbacks: global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, recovering to within a fraction of 2019's 73.4 years. This recovery represents a genuine achievement in public health, according to the UN's World Health Organization, which released its latest Global Health Estimates covering trends in death and disability from 2000 to 2023. Yet the full picture is more complex. Healthy life expectancy—the years people actually spend in good health—has recovered more slowly, reaching only 62.8 years in 2023, still 0.4 years short of pre-pandemic levels. The gap reveals an urgent challenge ahead: extending not just lifespan, but healthspan.

Behind these figures lies a profound shift in what threatens human health worldwide. For the first time in 2023, communicable diseases accounted for less than half of all deaths in low-income countries, marking a milestone in what the WHO calls the "global epidemiological transition." Noncommunicable diseases now cause 74 percent of global deaths—up from 58 percent in 2000—with cardiovascular disease leading the burden. Ischaemic heart disease alone caused approximately 9.5 million deaths in 2023. Meanwhile, dementia has risen dramatically, jumping from the 19th leading cause of death globally in 2000 to the fifth by 2023, with deaths tripling over that span.

These patterns vary sharply by region. While many parts of the world have reduced cardiovascular burden since 2000, the Western Pacific and Southeast Asia regions saw individual risk rise—a reminder that progress remains uneven. The WHO emphasizes that these estimates do more than document trends; they give countries concrete evidence to shape health policies and priorities tailored to their populations' actual needs.
quick_facts: Global life expectancy: 73.3 years in 2023, nearly back to 2019 level
Healthy life expectancy still 0.4 years below pre-pandemic 2019 level
First time: communicable diseases now cause less than half of deaths in low-income countries
Dementia deaths tripled from 2000 to 2023, rising to fifth leading cause
Noncommunicable diseases caused 74 percent of all deaths in 2023
